**Direct answer:** The evidence doesn't settle the exact day. Construction was completed in **1952**, in October. Wikipedia's infobox says **October 9, 1952**, but its own text says the headquarters was declared complete on **October 10, 1952**. October 10, 1952 is probably the better date, because that text cites a New York Times article of that date, "Work Completed on U.N. Buildings." I did not open that article.

**Claims and sources**

- The UN itself says only that construction "began on UN Day (24 October) 1949 and was completed in 1952." It gives no month or day.
  - https://www.un.org/en/visit/about-us
- The infobox on Wikipedia's page for the headquarters lists the completion date as October 9, 1952.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations
- The body of the same Wikipedia page says "The Manhattan headquarters was declared complete on October 10, 1952."
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations
- The same Wikipedia page gives the groundbreaking as September 14, 1948. The UN's visitor page gives a start of 24 October 1949, which is the date of the cornerstone ceremony. This is a separate discrepancy and doesn't affect the completion date.
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretariat_Building

**Gaps**
- The only source with an exact day is Wikipedia, which contradicts itself. I found no primary source, such as the New York Times article or a UN document, that gives the day.
- A third site I read (classicnewyorkhistory.com) says only that the headquarters was "constructed in 1952."
- "Complete" also depends on what you count. The Secretariat was finished earlier, and the Library (1961) and South Annex (1981–82) came later.

Sources:
- [Visitors Services, United Nations](https://www.un.org/en/visit/about-us)
- [Headquarters of the United Nations, Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_of_the_United_Nations)
- [United Nations Secretariat Building, Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretariat_Building)
- [History Of The United Nations Headquarters In New York, ClassicNewYorkHistory.com](https://classicnewyorkhistory.com/history-of-the-united-nations-headquarters-in-new-york/)
